setting.label: 1910–1928 CE · Four dated narrative sections
setting.note: The four printed section dates are 7 April 1928, 2 June 1910, 6 April 1928 and 8 April 1928, in narrative order. This is the bounding range of those four days, not continuous action or the range of every flashback or the later Compson Appendix.

description: Retells William Faulkner’s The Sound and the Fury through its four dated sections: Benjy’s sensory memories, Quentin’s last day at Harvard, Jason’s grievances and theft of Caddy’s financial support, and the Easter Sunday third-person narrative centered in part on Dilsey. Reconstructs the Compson family’s history, Caddy and her daughter Miss Quentin, the Gibson family’s labor and the final carriage scene, distinguishing the chronology of events from each narrator’s claims and the later Compson Appendix.
